audit_implementation.duplicate_detection: temporary on-disk SQLite tables store complete serialized source rows and unique station/timestamp keys
audit_implementation.commit_interval: at most 10000 input rows per transaction batch
audit_implementation.rollback_behavior: rollback is attempted only when SQLite reports an active transaction; cleanup failures are attached to the original exception

status_definitions.PASS: The specified check completed and met its stated technical criterion.
status_definitions.WARNING: Audit completed, but quality, provenance, or scientific questions remain.
status_definitions.FAIL: A required check failed or the audit could not complete.
status_definitions.NOT_CHECKED: No evidence was available or the check was outside this audit.

normalization.reason: No verified site mapping or confirmed source timezone was supplied. Do not infer stable gauge IDs, timezones, quality flags, or vertical datums.

limitations: Audit success is not scientific validation or readiness for hydraulic modelling.
No missing measurements are imputed and no suspicious or duplicate record is removed.
Timestamp timezone is not inferred; interval calculations use parsed source timestamps.
Station names and administrative codes do not independently authenticate physical gauge identity.
Catalog access labels do not establish licensing or unrestricted reuse rights.
recommended_next_steps: Obtain authoritative station IDs and provider documentation for field semantics and QC.
Confirm source timezone, units, vertical datum, coordinates, basin assignment, and reuse terms.
Review reported gaps, duplicates, outliers, and metadata inconsistencies with the data provider.
Only then prepare a normalized derivative with source-row traceability and explicit quality flags.
